find: return pinsText.replace(line, (_all, before: string, after: string) => before + sha + after)
replace: return JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(pinsText.replace(line, (_all, before: string, after: string) => before + sha + after)), null, 2) + '\n'
title: gives back the committed bytes where the fingerprint has not moved
why: The writer going back to JSON.stringify: the committed file is in Prettier's form, so every run would reformat lines it did not change and lint would fail.

title: refuses a file with no fingerprint line, or with two
why: Two fingerprint lines accepted and both rewritten: the file would be changed where the writer could not say which line it meant.

title: changes the fingerprint and no other byte of the file
why: The pattern taking in the whitespace after the value: the writer would drop the newline and the indent of the line after the fingerprint.
